title: TSLA的风险回报比已经（悄悄地）变了...

keyPoints.text: Morgan Stanley assigned Tesla a $475 price target for year-end 2026 under the condition that its robotaxi Cybercab operates smoothly.
Tesla's Cybercab possesses substantial manufacturing and operational cost advantages over Waymo, with Cybercab production cost under $20,000.
Tesla's rapid deployment and scaling of autonomous vehicles creates a network flywheel effect that outpaces Waymo's slow expansion.

Tesla's autonomous ride-hailing flywheel is scaling in Austin with 69 vehicles deployed, where faster rollout increases users, app revenue, and fleet size, creating an operational advantage that competitors like Waymo cannot match.

Tesla accepted massive upfront risks by eliminating steering wheels, pedals, mirrors, lidar, and HD maps in favor of an eight-camera vision-only AI approach, whereas Waymo relied on a safer initial setup with 4,000 cars backed by Google, yielding limited returns and high ongoing capital dependency.

Tesla's probability of achieving full self-driving success is substantially higher than three to five years ago, yet its share price around $300 remains below its 2021 high of over $400, reflecting unrewarded operational progress through high builder risks.

Jeremy Grantham forecasted a 75% plunge in the S&P 500 and previously predicted Tesla would fail within two years in 2019, after which Tesla rose tenfold; he argued Musk promotes stock to fund R&D before delivering constructive milestones, which Musk countered by stating Grantham is a short-seller/investor rather than a 'builder'.

Grantham gained fame and wealth by shorting Enron, but acting as a true builder—or investing in Tesla either as a long-term shareholder or for a 1-to-2-year horizon on robotaxi price upside—requires bearing substantial execution failure risk.

SpaceX was valued at approximately $400 billion to $500 billion prior to going public and before acquiring xAI, despite operating at an ongoing loss, illustrating an infinite P/E ratio where investors accept a near-infinite timeframe to recoup costs in exchange for massive builder upside.

calls.thesis: Tesla is more worth buying as execution risks diminish while its valuation upside remains intact.
risks: Risk that Cybercab / robotaxi fails to operate smoothly

tickerSentiment.why: The speaker argues that Waymo cannot compete with Cybercab and will remain an external capital-dependent business generating questionable returns for Google.
The creator argues that Tesla is increasingly worth buying because its technological and operational risks are declining while its underlying value remains unchanged.
The speaker views Tesla's FSD progress and Cybercab rollout as proving high probability of success while the stock remains undervalued relative to its 2021 peak.
The speaker questions whether Google can achieve real returns from continuing to subsidize Waymo in autonomous driving or compete aggressively against Tesla and Meta.
The creator references Meta in passing as a strong competitive benchmark in personal AI assistants against Google.
The speaker cites Grantham's warning on CNBC that the S&P 500 would plunge 75 percent.
Grantham made his fortune and built his reputation by correctly identifying fraud and shorting Enron.

The speaker argues Tesla is even more worth buying because its technological and operational risks have dropped significantly while its underlying valuation and long-term potential have not decreased.
The speaker questions whether Google can ever get any return from Waymo despite pouring continuous capital into it and failing to aggressively compete with Tesla or Meta.
The creator argues that Tesla successfully reduced its FSD autonomous driving risks through technological execution, proving its capabilities with real-world deployments.

The speaker argues that Tesla's probability of solving autonomous driving is much higher than years ago while its stock price is still only around 300 compared to over 400 at its 2021 high, showing that execution risks have almost been surmounted.

sentences: The speaker notes that market commentator Jeremy Grantham previously warned on CNBC that the S&P 500 would plunge 75%.
According to the speaker, Grantham predicted in 2019 that Tesla would fail within two years, after which Tesla's stock rose tenfold.
The speaker mentions that Grantham built his reputation by shorting Enron and possesses estimated assets around 10 billion.
Morgan Stanley assigned Tesla a year-end 2026 target price of $475 under the condition that Cybercab robotaxi operates smoothly.
The speaker notes that an operational failure by 2026 remains an explicit execution risk to that Morgan Stanley target price scenario.

SpaceX was valued at approximately 400 billion to 500 billion prior to going public and before acquiring xAI despite running continuous operating losses, which the speaker uses to illustrate an infinite price-to-earnings dynamic where investors accept long recoupment periods.
The speaker argues that Tesla is more worth buying now because its operational and autonomous execution risks have fallen while its underlying valuation upside remains intact.
The presenter states that Cybercab's production cost is under $20,000, which is lower than Tesla's own cost to build a Model Y.

By comparison, the speaker asserts that Waymo's vehicle build cost exceeded $100,000 per unit when manufactured with Jaguar, and subsequent contract manufacturing with Zeekr remains structurally higher than Cybercab due to LiDAR and HD map requirements.
The speaker contrasts Waymo's fleet size of 4,000 vehicles after 10 years with Tesla reaching over 500 vehicles in just over a year while growing at 17% per week.
In Austin, Tesla recently added over 20 vehicles to reach 69 vehicles deployed.

The speaker argues this scaling creates a local flywheel where faster vehicle deployment in a city attracts more app users and generates revenue to fund further car deployments, leaving Waymo unable to compete.

Tesla took on significant structural risk by removing the steering wheel, pedals, mirrors, LiDAR, and HD maps in favor of eight vision cameras and AI, whereas the speaker views Waymo as relying on Google subsidies without bearing comparable risks.

The creator observes that despite Tesla's probability of solving autonomous driving being much higher than three to five years ago, the stock price around $300 remains well below its 2021 high of over $400.

No external corroboration was provided for the Morgan Stanley price target cutoff or the exact timing of Jeremy Grantham's CNBC interview.
Details of Waymo's historical capital burn and exact revenue return metrics to Google were asserted qualitatively without official financial filings.
